Heater 9 (marker: square with backslash hatch, '⊘') is the topmost/leftmost of the 9 heater curves and is visually separable from the other 8 heaters across its full range, reaching CHF at the lowest wall superheat. Points read by eye against a pixel-calibrated log-log grid (calibrated from axis tick marks at 1/10/100 on both axes, since axis labels are part of the raster image with no PDF text layer).

series.label: Heater 1
series.notes: Heater 1 (open circle marker) is consistently the bottom-most/right-most of the 9 heater curves (worst boiling performance, reaching the shared CHF value at the highest wall superheat, ~41 C vs ~21-27 C for the other heaters). Distinguishable at both curve extremes and traceable through the dense mid-range cluster as the lower-right envelope of the bundle. Read by eye against the calibrated log-log grid.

series.label: Heater 5
series.notes: Heater 5 (plus marker, '+') starts as a visually distinct curve at low wall superheat (highest q'' for a given dT_sat among the low-DeltaT points) but its markers merge into the dense central bundle of overlapping heater curves beyond dT_sat ~2.5 C and cannot be reliably followed further; only the distinguishable early portion is reported here rather than guessing its path through the bundle.

series.label: Heaters 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 (merged, indistinguishable)
series.notes: Heaters 2 (square), 3 (diamond), 4 (down-triangle), 6 (up-triangle), 7 (x), and 8 (square with cross-hatch) all fall into a single tightly overlapping band of markers/lines for nearly the entire curve (visually inseparable), so per the task instructions these are reported as one merged representative curve running through the middle of that band rather than fabricating 6 separate traces. Heaters 2 and 4 coincide at the very lowest point (~1.15 C, 0.62 W/cm^2); the merged path terminates near the shared CHF value at dT_sat ~23-27 C, consistent with the visual fan-out at CHF where this cluster reaches CHF between heater 9 (~21 C) and heaters 1/2/3 individually resolved near CHF (~33-41 C).
